full_judgment: 3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that defendant 1 Shankar Kumar Mondal was owner in possession in 1.9950 acres out of 3.10 acres of land appertaining to RS plot 1112 of RS khatian 107 by virtue of three registered documents. He expressed his desire to sell the suit property to which plaintiff responded and the consideration money was fixed at Taka 18,00,000 (eighteen lac). The conversation of such agreement was done by the plaintiff with defendant 1 in presence of his father defendant 2 and since the necessary documents were not in the custody of defendant 1 and the record of right also was not prepared in his name it took time to get the document registered. But instead of that event an agreement was executed between plaintiff and defendant 1 for want of urgent cash. For such reason 5,00,000 (five lac) taka as earnest money was given to defendant 1 and on 1-6-2009 the agreement was registered. There was a stipulation in the agreement that after receiving the rest 13,00,000 (thirteen lac) taka from the plaintiff within a year defendant 1 shall register the document failing which plaintiff shall get the same registered through Court. But within that period defendant asked the plaintiff to wait for getting registration of the document upon various pretexts. Meanwhile defendant 2 who is the father of defendant 1 filed Title Suit No. 98 of 2009 on 16-6-2009 for declaration that defendant 1 is his benamder. Plaintiff of this suit also filed written statement in that suit. However, subsequently defendant 1 delayed the execution and registration in collusion with defendant 2. In such circumstance plaintiff sent a legal notice by registered post on 13-5-2010 requesting defendant 1 to execute and register the document within 30-5-2010. But defendant 1 neither registered the document nor received the rest amount of the consideration money. Hence the suit was filed by depositing the rest 13,00,000 (thirteen lac) taka to the Court and prayed for decree of the same.
